summary: Both round-1 majors are genuinely closed — verified by re-running the mutations myself in an isolated copy of the repo, not by trusting the summary. (1) Test_processData_versionChange_reresolvesOrderColumn now discriminates all three candidate orders: with pids 3003/4004 swapped so the low pid carries the winning state, dropping `orderConfigured = false` while KEEPING the seed restore now produces a real failure ('900' is not less than '710') where in round 1 the whole suite stayed green. (2) The fourth subtest 'empty value at zero width is not an error' now pins the guard's placement inside `if valuelen > width`: hoisting the guard above the truncation branch fails that subtest with 'Received unexpected error: zero or negative width, skip', where in round 1 the hoist survived. All four remaining minors were applied as agreed (require.NoError on all three processData returns, the pre-boundary bracketing assertion, beforeBoundaryRows/afterBoundaryRows renaming, the unused v.Aligned = true lines dropped). I re-ran the full 7-mutation matrix independently — all 7 detected, matching the reported results exactly — and added three mutations of my own. Two of mine survived, but they turn out to be dead assignments in the implementation rather than a test gap (see the single minor below); the third (removing the `linesPrinted := repeatHeaderAfter` seed) is caught by 17 existing golden tests. Suite is deterministic: zeroWidthGuard passes 300x standalone, the full report package passes 12x with -count=1 and 3x under -race; go vet clean; report/testdata untouched. Zero critical, zero major.

findings.location: report/report.go:287-288 (v.ColsWidth = map[int]int{} and v.Cols = nil inside the versionChanged block)
findings.issue: Mutation testing of the new suite shows these two assignments are not pinned by any test — and cannot be, because they have no observable effect. Verified: deleting either line individually leaves the entire ./report/... suite green (both mutations SURVIVED). The reason is structural, not a coverage hole: formatStatSample (report.go:513-523) unconditionally overwrites both view.ColsWidth and view.Cols whenever Aligned is false, and it is the first thing that runs on the next sample after the version-change branch does `continue`. Nothing reads v.ColsWidth or v.Cols between the reset and that overwrite — printStatHeader and printStatSample are both downstream of formatStatSample, and v is a by-value local, so no external observer exists. The `v.Aligned = false` line alone carries the whole behaviour (dropping it fails all three version-change tests). The code comment claims the pair is cleared 'so the gap until the next sample carries no known-wrong layout', but there is no gap in which anything can read it.
findings.recommendation: No test change. This is an implementation observation for the code reviewer: either drop the two assignments and keep `v.Aligned = false` alone (the minimal change that produces the behaviour the three tests pin), or, if they are deliberately kept as defence against a future reader of the layout being added between the reset and formatStatSample, adjust the comment to say so explicitly — 'defensive; currently unobservable because formatStatSample rewrites both on the next sample' — so a later reader does not mistake them for load-bearing code and a later mutation-testing pass does not re-flag them. Do not add a white-box test asserting the intermediate map is empty: it would pin a private intermediate state, not behaviour.
